ratings.reason: The quote describes preserving functional and geometric properties during style transformation, but it does not show an automatically computed protected subset of the artifact or a generation-time mechanism that forbids modifying that subset. This is closer to property-preserving transformation than Protected Region. With no fuller evidence available, the required structural signature is unsupported.

ratings.reason: This is a strong instance: functionality-aware segmentation partitions the 3D model into functional and aesthetic segments, and modification is confined to aesthetic segments so functional ones remain unaffected. The title supplies the segmentation step and the quote supplies the protection during modification. The mechanism is central and consequential, although the limited evidence does not explain exactly how segmentation or non-modification is implemented. The partition-and-protect strategy transfers well beyond 3D fabrication, even if identifying functionality is domain-specific.

The quote plainly demonstrates both required components. Provenance automatically partitions the drawing—user-authored strokes constitute the protected subset—and generation uses a penalty against moving, overdrawing, or occluding them. This is exceptionally clear and readily transferable to text, code, layout, and other co-created artifacts. Representativeness stops short of 5 because the paper's stated contribution concerns perceptions of agency rather than Protected Region itself, but the system mechanism is an unambiguous exemplar.
